question: What is the RHB 2024 rate for providing and fixing a 190 mm CP brass rain shower of superior quality?
answer: Item S-2.33.18, '190 mm rain shower', a child of S-2.33 (Providing and fixing Superior quality (Jaguar Continental) CP Brass fittings complete as per direction of EI): Rs. 5290.00 per Each.
notes: Child row text is only '190 mm rain shower'; the 'superior quality CP brass' meaning lives in parent 2.33. Neighbours: shower arm 1151.00, hand shower 1733.00.

question: What basic material rate does the RHB schedule use for plastic emulsion paint?
answer: General basic rate code G-835, 'Plastic emulsion paint': Rs. 285.00 per Litre.
notes: Material rate in the G chapter. Do not confuse with B-12.41 (wall painting with plastic emulsion paint), which is a per-Sqm work item.

question: What does RHB allow for providing and fixing an IS:3564 marked universal hydraulic door closer with an extruded aluminium section body and double speed adjustment?
answer: Item B-8.34: IS:3564 marked aluminium extruded section body tubular type universal hydraulic door closer with double speed adjustment, with accessories and screws: Rs. 1393.00 Each.
notes: Near-misses: B-8.21 (aluminium die cast body door closer, 705.00, page B-38, PDF p96) and G material codes 2456 (bottle type, 1050.00) and 7060 (tubular aluminium, 1600.00).

question: What is the rate for supplying and fixing an ISI marked 16 amp flush type non-modular switch?
answer: Item E-7.2: P & F ISI marked (IS:3854) 16 amp flush type non modular switch, CM/L no. printed, polycarbonate or fire resistant ABS: Rs. 50.00 Each.
notes: E-7.1 is the 6 amp version at 23.00. Page opens chapter E-7 (Electrical accessories) with the chapter title printed at the bottom of the page.

question: For road work, what is the RHB rate for a tack coat of RS-1 bitumen emulsion applied at 0.30 to 0.35 kg per sqm on a cement concrete pavement surface?
answer: Item R-3.2(iv): tack coat with bitumen emulsion (RS-1) using emulsion pressure distributor at 0.30 to 0.35 kg per sqm on prepared non-bituminous surfaces (cement concrete pavement): Rs. 19.94 per Sqm.
notes: R chapter uses roman sub-items and the text layer separates descriptions from rates, so the rate must be matched by layout. Siblings: (i) 14.00, (ii) 17.00, (iii) 17.00.

question: What is the RHB rate per sqm for 60 mm thick M-30 precast concrete interlocking paving blocks in grey natural cement colour, laid on an average 50 mm coarse sand bed with joints filled with fine sand?
answer: Item B-11.26: precast concrete interlocking blocks of M 30 grade, 60 mm thick (BS 6717:2001), grey cement natural colour, laid on average 50 mm thick bed of coarse sand with joints filled with fine sand: Rs. 693.00 per Sqm.
notes: Near-misses: B-11.27 pavers in any colour (995.00, same page), the R chapter interlocking block pavement items (page R-16, PDF p670) and G material code 8689 (578.00).

question: What is the rate per metre for a 20 mm OD PE-AL-PE composite pressure pipe installed concealed in the wall, including cutting chases and making good?
answer: Item S-2.30.2, '1620 (20mm OD) pipe', under S-2.30 (PE-AL-PE composite pressure pipes, concealed installation including cutting chases and making good the walls): Rs. 241.00 per Metre.
notes: Identical child text under three parents: exposed on wall S-2.29.2 = 219.00 (S-19), concealed S-2.30.2 = 241.00, external S-2.31..2 = 200.00 (printed with a double dot). Only the parent tells them apart.

question: What is the rate per metre for a 300 mm x 50 mm x 1.6 mm perforated hot dipped galvanized cable tray suspended from the ceiling?
answer: Item E-12.5.4, '300mm x 50mm x 1.6mm', under E-12.5 (supply, fabricating and installing perforated hot dipped galvanized iron cable tray, perforation not more than 17.5%, suspended from ceiling with GI suspenders): Rs. 1053.00 per Mtr.
notes: Same size row exists under E-12.6.4 (perforated powder coated MS tray, 907.00) and E-12.7.4 (HDG tray with rungs, 826.00, page E-65). Material and type are only in the parent.

question: What is the rate per cum for a WBM Grading 2 sub-base/base using crusher broken aggregate, laid by mechanical means?
answer: Item R-2.2, sub-item 2) WBM Grading 2, II Using crusher broken aggregate, (B) By mechanical means: Rs. 1112.00 per Cum.
notes: Four-level nesting (2.2 > 2) Grading 2 > II crusher broken > (B) mechanical). Siblings: hand broken manual 913.00, hand broken mechanical 786.00, crusher broken manual 1240.00. Text layer detaches labels from rates.

question: Under the water supply works, what is the rate for a 2.2 kW (3.0 HP) submersible dewatering pump set?
answer: Item S-5.57.11, '2.2 KW (3.0 HP)', under the submersible dewatering pump set description printed as row S-5.57.8: Rs. 88983.00 Each.
notes: Trap: S-5.57.1 is also '2.2 KW (3.0 HP)' but belongs to the submersible monoblock pump (40013.00). The dewatering parent is itself numbered like a child (5.57.8). E-21.8.3 (3.0 HP dewatering motor pump set, 46149.0, page E-129) is a cross-chapter near-miss.

question: What is the rate for a concealed four-way divertor of superior quality?
answer: Item S-2.22.3, printed '(-do-) Four way (-do-)'. Read with S-2.22.2 '(-do-) Concealed Five-way divertors' and parent S-2.22 'P & F Divertors of superior quality and approved make', it is a concealed four-way divertor: Rs. 2198.00 Each.
notes: The row text is only '(-do-) Four way (-do-)'; the ditto chain must be resolved through 2.22.2. Five-way is 2138.00 and three-way 2048.00, so four-way is priced above five-way.

question: If grade 'AA' glazed stoneware pipes are used instead of grade 'A' for a 150 mm dia drainage line, what rate per metre should be taken?
answer: Base item S-3.1.2 (150mm dia glazed S.W. pipe grade 'A', laid and jointed with excavation and refilling up to 1.2 m depth) is Rs. 413.00 per Mtr. The note under item 3.1 says add 5% if grade 'AA' S.W. pipes are used: 413.00 x 1.05 = Rs. 433.65 per Mtr.
notes: The modifier is an unnumbered note between items 3.1.7 and 3.2. Note 2 (deduct 5% if jointing in CM 1:3) is a distractor; chapter S-3 notes above the table also say depth beyond 1.2 m is paid extra.

question: What rate per metre applies for excavating a trench in ordinary rock for a 150 mm pipe when the trench is 2.5 m deep?
answer: Base item B-1.8.1.2 (ordinary rock, pipes exceeding 80 mm but not exceeding 300 mm dia, depth up to 1.5 m) is Rs. 429.00 per Mtr. Item B-1.9 adds 104% over the corresponding basic item for depth exceeding 1.5 m but not exceeding 3 m: extra 446.16, total Rs. 875.16 per Mtr.
notes: Combines a child row on B-2 with a percentage-extra item on B-3. The soil equivalent (B-1.6) is only 1.41%, so picking the wrong extra item gives a very different answer.

question: We are pricing 200 m of 150 mm DI potable water main. How much more would K-9 grade pipe cost than K-7 grade, per metre and for the whole run?
answer: S-5.1.3 (DI K-7 grade S&S pipe, 150 mm) is Rs. 2189.00 per RMT and S-5.2.2 (DI K-9 grade, 150 mm) is Rs. 2509.00 per RMT. Difference Rs. 320.00 per RMT, i.e. Rs. 64000.00 for 200 m (earthwork excluded in both).
notes: Both rows are bare '150 mm' children; K-7 vs K-9 appears only in the long parents 5.1 and 5.2. S-6 sewer DI K-7 with HAC lining (page S-122) is a different item.

question: Using RHB basic material rates, what is the extra material cost of upsizing a 50 m GI pipe run from 20 mm to 25 mm dia?
answer: G code 1546 'G.I. pipes 20 mm dia' is Rs. 205.00 per Mtr. and G code 1547 'G.I. pipes 25 mm dia' is Rs. 290.00 per Mtr. Difference Rs. 85.00 per Mtr., i.e. Rs. 4250.00 for 50 m.
notes: Uses G chapter material rates, not the S chapter laid-in-place GI pipe items.

question: What is item S-5.62.1.4 and what is its rate?
answer: S-5.62.1.4 is a 150 mm dia CI double flanged swing type Non Return Valve (NRV), Class PN 1.0 (S-5.62 > 5.62.1 Class PN 1.0), conforming to IS 5312 (Part 1), rates exclusive of tail piece/dismantling joints and earth work: Rs. 14672.00 Each.
notes: Row text is just '150 mm dia'; meaning comes from two parent levels. Close neighbours: CI sluice valve 150 mm HW 14644.00 (S-5.60.1.4), dual plate check valve 150 mm 13014.00 (S-5.63.1.4).

question: What does item E-12.11 cover, and what is its rate?
answer: E-12.11 is supply and fixing of a cable route marker: 10 cm x 10 cm x 5 mm thick (or 10 cm dia) GI plate with inscription, bolted/welded to 35 x 35 x 5 mm angle iron 60 cm long, fixed in ground in CC 1:3:6. Rate Rs. 388.00 Each.
notes: Standalone item with the rate on the parent row (no children).

question: What is the RHB rate per metre for a pressed steel door frame to IS 4351 in Profile D?
answer: Not in the schedule. Item B-9.4 (pressed steel door frames to IS 4351) gives only Profile B (Rs. 432.00 per Mtr.), Profile C (Rs. 460.00 per Mtr.) and Profile E (Rs. 488.00 per Mtr.); there is no Profile D rate.
notes: Near-miss variant: the parent and other profiles exist, so a system must not pick or interpolate a neighbouring profile.

question: What is the rate for item 1.1.2?
answer: Ambiguous: item numbers restart in each chapter. 1.1.2 exists as S-1.1.2 (Indian type squatting pan, size 510 mm, Rs. 1208.00 Each), E-1.1.2 (wiring of light/fan point, medium point up to 6 mtr, Rs. 578.00 per P. point) and H-1.1.2 (compost, Rs. 650.00 per Cum.). Ask which chapter is meant.
notes: Expected behaviour is to ask for the chapter or list all three; picking one is wrong. B has B-1.1.1 but no 1.1.2; R and L use other numbering. All three pages are DEV pages.

question: What is the rate for a 500 mm dia ferro-cement manhole cover with a 12 kg CI frame, medium duty (15 MT centre point load)?
answer: Item S-3.33.2, printed '500mm dia 12 Kg.-do-15 MT centre point load (medium duty)', where '-do-' stands for 'C.I. frame to with stand' from S-3.33.1, under S-3.33 (Supplying and fixing Ferro-cement cover with C.I. frame for chambers & man holes): Rs. 2160.00 Each.
notes: Ditto sits mid-row; its meaning comes from sibling 3.33.1 (450 mm light duty, 1288.00).

question: A masonry septic tank for 20 users is needed, but 0.5 m longer than the standard RHB size. What rate should be used?
answer: Base item S-3.28.2 (septic tank size 230 x 110 x 150 cm, for 20 users) is Rs. 35868.00 Each. The note under S-3.28 says add or subtract proportionately for every 0.5 m increase or decrease: length 12.5%, breadth and depth 18% each. For +0.5 m length: 35868.00 x 1.125 = Rs. 40351.50 Each.
notes: The note is printed in the item-number column as 'Note :-' right after 3.28.3; breadth/depth use 18%, not 12.5%.

question: What is the RHB horticulture rate for supplying neem cake?
answer: Item H-1.1.5 'Neem Cake', under H-1.1 (supply of dry manure including loading, unloading, transportation and stacking at site): Rs. 1250.00 Per 50 Kg Bag.
notes: Unit is per 50 kg bag, unlike the other manures in H-1.1 which are per Cum. (e.g. compost 650.00). Other 'neem' mentions in H are trees.

question: What is the RHB rate for supplying a hazard marker of 2 mm MS sheet, 300 x 300 mm, on channel posts with reflective discs?
answer: Item R-6.17: supply of Hazard Marker made of 2 mm thick M.S. sheet size 300x300x3 mm framed with angle iron 25x25x3 mm, fixed on channel posts 75x40x6 mm with hold fast, painted white with 6 Nos. 5 cm dia reflective sheet discs: Rs. 760.00 Each.
notes: R chapter page whose text layer puts all rates before the descriptions.

question: What is the rate for new wiring of a twin control light point in recessed PVC conduit, medium point up to 6 m?
answer: Item E-1.2.2 'Medium point (up to 6 mtr.)', under E-1.2 (wiring of twin control light point with 1.5 sq. mm FR PVC copper conductor and earth conductor in recessed ISI marked PVC conduit, with modular boxes and two-way modular switches): Rs. 1137.00 per P. point.
notes: The child text recurs under E-1.1 (single light point, 578.00), E-1.3, E-1.5 (rewiring), E-1.6.2 (rewiring twin control, 877.00) and E-3.2 (surface UPVC trunking, page E-7).

question: For 150 m of boundary fencing on a road job, how much more would 1.8 m high GI barbed wire fencing cost than the 1.2 m high version?
answer: R-6.11 (G.I barbed wire fencing 1.8 m high, 2.4 m RCC posts, 12 horizontal lines) is Rs. 674.00 per Running m and R-6.10 (1.2 m high, 1.8 m RCC posts, 9 horizontal lines) is Rs. 474.00 per Running m. Difference Rs. 200.00 per running metre, i.e. Rs. 30000.00 for 150 m.
notes: R chapter text layer detaches rates from descriptions. R-1.4 (dismantling barbed wire fencing) is a lexical distractor.

question: What is the RHB basic rate for expanded polystyrene type SE?
answer: No rate is given. Code G-7091 'Expanded polystyrene type - SE' is listed with unit Sqm but its rate cell is blank. (Type N-Normal, code 7090, is Rs. 165.00 per Sqm.)
notes: Listed item with an empty rate cell; a system must not borrow 165.00 from the adjacent type N row.

question: What is item B-4.20 and how is it applied?
answer: B-4.20 'Add extra over for both side jali' is 20% (unit Sqm.), an extra over the precast cement concrete jali items B-4.19 (50 mm 756.00, 40 mm 981.00, 30 mm 625.00 per Sqm) for both-side jali.
notes: A percentage item that only makes sense with the preceding item 4.19. The 40 mm jali (981.00) is printed dearer than the 50 mm (756.00).

question: What's the rate for item 4.1.1 in the RHB BSR 2024?
answer: Ambiguous: 4.1.1 exists in two chapters. S-4.1.1 is construction of tube well, nominal bore 150 mm dia, Rs. 994.00 per Mtr; E-4.1.1 is FR PVC insulated unsheathed flexible copper conductor 1 x 1.5 sq.mm, Rs. 22.00 per Mtr. Ask which chapter (Sanitary or Electrical) is meant.
notes: Expected behaviour is to ask or list both. B-4.1 and H-4.1 exist but have no 4.1.1 child; R uses roman sub-items.

question: What is the rate for an exposed WVC toilet paper holder, 1st quality ISI marked, 150 x 150 mm?
answer: Item S-1.53.4, printed '(-do-) exposed (-do-)'. Read with S-1.53.3 'WVC (1stquality, ISI Marked) recessed size 150x150mm' under S-1.53 (P & F Toilet Paper Holder with rod), it is the WVC exposed 150x150 mm holder: Rs. 238.00 Each.
notes: Double ditto: both material and size come from the previous sibling. The recessed version (1.53.3) is 305.00.

question: If, with the Engineer-in-Charge's approval, M15 nominal mix (1:2:4) concrete up to plinth level is done without a mechanical mixer, what rate per cum applies?
answer: Base item B-3.1.1 (M15 grade nominal mix 1:2:4, 20 mm aggregate, all work up to plinth level) is Rs. 4393.00 per Cum. Chapter B-3 Note 4: where mechanical mixer and vibrator are not used, rates are reduced by 15% for mechanical mixer and 10% for vibrator. Without the mixer: 4393.00 x 0.85 = Rs. 3734.05 per Cum.
notes: Chapter-opening note printed above the table. B-3.2.2 (M15 in walls etc., 4778.00) is a distractor.

question: What hire charge per day does the RHB schedule take for a 0.14 cum concrete mixer?
answer: General basic rate code G-2, 'Hire charges of Concrete Mixer 0.14 cubic Mtr.': Rs. 1300.00 Per day.
notes: Code 2 in the G chapter (hire charges of plants and machinery); note the code 'G-2' is not the page label G-2.

question: What is the RHB rate for laying Mexican (carpet) grass tiles of 2 ft x 2 ft for garden development?
answer: Item H-3.1.5: 'Maxican(Carpet) grass tiles (2'X2' size) for development of garden, including levelling of soil and spreading of manure': Rs. 400.00 per Sqm.
notes: Printed as 'Maxican' (typo). Unit is per Sqm while the lawn items 3.1.1 to 3.1.3 are per 100 Sqm. Selection No. 1 grass tiles (3.1.4) are 250.00.

question: What is the RHB rate for mowing lawns with power machines?
answer: Item H-2.1.4(b) 'With power machines', under H-2.1.4 'Mowing manually / with power machines' (H-2.1 Maintenance of Lawns): Rs. 700.00 Per Hect.
notes: Child (b) row says only 'With power machines.'; manual mowing (a) is 1300.00 Per Hect.

question: We need to lay a new 500 sqm lawn with grass planted in rows 15 cm apart each way. What would it cost at RHB rates, excluding manure and extra earth?
answer: Item H-3.1.1 (laying of lawns, in rows 15 cm apart in either direction) is Rs. 1621.00 per 100 Sqm. For 500 sqm: 5 x 1621.00 = Rs. 8105.00. Cost of manure or extra good earth is paid separately as stated in parent H-3.1.
notes: Unit is per 100 Sqm, a unit-conversion trap.

question: What is item S-1.13 and its rate?
answer: S-1.13: 'Add extra if C.I.P trap is used in place of Vitreous china P trap for W.C.': Rs. 511.00 Each.
notes: An add-extra item that modifies W.C. items; the vitreous china P trap itself is S-1.12 at 342.00.

question: What was the RHB 2013 basic daily wage for a Beldar?
answer: Not answerable from this document: it is the RHB Basic Schedule of Rates 2024 and gives no 2013 rates. The 2024 rate for a Beldar (G code 114) is Rs. 500.00 Per day.
notes: False premise (wrong edition year).
